Contribution per trip vs. the bar, by payer

Per-driver profitability against the bar

Native per-driver totals from RECDAY (pay + fuel), no cross-broker allocation needed. Same bar and contribution logic as the payer table.

Per-payer profitability against the bar

Direct cost allocated at the driver-day level: each driver's daily pay+fuel divided by that day's trip count, applied per broker — the finest grain the source data supports (no per-trip pay/fuel breakdown exists). Contribution/Trip = Revenue/Trip − Direct Cost/Trip. Margin vs Bar = Contribution/Trip − the bar. Positive means that payer's average trip covers its share of company overhead and then some; this is a break-even/pricing benchmark, not a recommendation to drop any payer.

The bar over time

Week-to-week movement here is real — it's driven by actual paid-trip volume (the indirect $ pool itself is smoothed to remove cash-basis lumpiness, but the denominator isn't). A rising bar generally means volume dropped, not that costs spiked.
